title: Repair: control-plane claim rehydration dropping tenant claims causing RBAC binding omission and audit gaps
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a private control-plane failover scenario we observed tenant identity claims periodically failing to rehydrate into the local auth cache. When claims are omitted, RBAC rolebindings for ephemeral sessions are not created and audit events that should have been emitted for authorization checks are missing. Several enterprise customers (notably CUST-19872) reported 'user not authorized' errors followed by truncated audit trails during maintenance windows. KMS unwrap attempts for tenant-wrapped secrets also saw a correlated 504 window.

Root cause hypothesis (current):
- The rehydration path that merges claims after keepalive/failover uses an optimistic merge that ignores empty/partial claim payloads when the control-plane is under pressure.
- An edge-case race between control-plane sync and local session creation causes a code path to skip RBAC reconciliation if the claim set has no 'roles' array (null vs empty array bug).
- Audit emitter filters out events if the session's canonical tenant_version is 0 (returned during transient rehydration).

Why urgent:
- Customer-facing outages and audit gaps are regulatory-impacting for customers on Private deployments.
- The bug can persist across restarts, requiring manual tenant re-sync for affected customers.

Reproduction notes (short):
1) Simulate control-plane failover (kill control-plane leader) while creating 50 concurrent sessions for a tenant with short-lived assertions.
2) Observe sessions that are created during the leader election window.
3) Check auth-cache: missing roles field and tenant_version==0 for subset of sessions.
4) Verify missing RBAC bindings (kubectl get rolebindings) and absent audit events in the audit-forwarder logs for the window.

Links: 
- Customer escalation: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/CUST-19872
- Postmortem/analysis draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Claim+Rehydration+Postmortem
- Preliminary runbook for mitigation: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Runbook+Claim+Rehydrate
- Github PR (fix branch): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9123

Decision trade-offs considered:
- Strict rehydration: apply full canonical merge that blocks session creation until claims are validated. Pro: correctness. Con: increases latency and may cause user-facing delays during failover for high-throughput customers.
- Opportunistic reconciliation (chosen): accept session creation but enqueue a fast synchronous reconciliation attempt for sessions missing claims, with bounded retry and circuit-breaker. Pro: minimizes user-visible latency while repairing RBAC and audit. Con: adds additional reconciliation complexity and a small window where audit events might be delayed (we will emit a pre-auth event to avoid total loss).

Mitigation & Patch plan (what we're shipping in priv-2026.03.2):
- Fix parsing bug: treat missing 'roles' as an empty array (strict schema enforcement).
- Change rehydration merge to mark tenant_version as invalid instead of zero; auditors will accept and force immediate reconciliation.
- Add synchronous reconcile path that runs before the first authorization check for sessions with tenant_version==invalid (fast-path, <200ms target).
- Emit a pre-authorization audit event whenever a session is created with a placeholder tenant_version to avoid silent audit drops.
- Add metrics and an alert: gauge for sessions_created_with_placeholder_claims and alert threshold >50/min per tenant.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (hotfix branch): cherry-pick to 2026-03-14 canary on two low-impact private clusters. Manual smoke tests and monitoring for 2 hours. (In progress)
- Stage 2: extend canary to three customer clusters including a default-enterprise cluster (2026-03-15 morning).
- Stage 3: full rollout to all private control-planes (2026-03-16) with 15-minute pause windows and rollback script ready.

Verification criteria (pre-merge & post-deploy):
- Unit tests cover parsing edge cases and tenant_version transitions.
- Integration test reproduces failure scenario in CI job infra/repro/claim-rehydrate (green).
- Canary metrics: sessions_created_with_placeholder_claims drops to 0 and audit events emitted for the previously-missing window.
- Customer validation: CUST-19872 confirms access restored and audit trails complete.

Follow-ups (post-hotpatch):
- Backfill audit events for affected window where possible (investigate audit-forwarder retention and reconstruct events).
- Long-term: design a centralized rehydration API with transactional guarantees and a non-blocking queue for reconciliation (ENG-Q3 initiative).
- Add an automated test harness that simulates control-plane leader election under concurrency and asserts no claim loss.

steps_to_reproduce: Deploy control-plane leader to a test cluster with tenancy assertions enabled.
Start 50 concurrent short-lived SSO sessions during a simulated leader failover (kill leader).
Query auth cache: check for sessions where 'roles' is null and tenant_version==0.
Attempt an RBAC protected action with affected sessions and observe 'forbidden' responses and missing audit records in audit-forwarder logs.
mitigation: Immediate mitigation applied: temporary operator script to force tenant re-sync for affected clusters (ops/tenant-resync.sh). This reduces customer impact until the hotpatch is applied. Ops notified customers and triggered manual re-sync for CUST-19872.
